title: Independence of affine ordinary tensor resolution comparison maps
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $M,N$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For each affine open $U$ set $A_U=\Gamma(Y,U)$, choose $A_U$-modules $MA_U,NA_U$ and $A_U$-linear equivalences $sM_U:MA_U\simeq\Gamma(U,M)$ and $sN_U:NA_U\simeq\Gamma(U,N)$, and choose a projective resolution $P_U\to MA_U$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module, def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Fix a K-flat cochain complex $K$ and a quasi-isomorphism $q:K\to M[0]$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For $n\ge0$ set $Q=H^{-n}(\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes N[0]))$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Suppose $c_U:H_n(P_U\otimes_{A_U}NA_U)\simeq\Gamma(U,Q)$ are $A_U$-linear equivalences. Assume that for every inclusion $V\subseteq U$ of affine opens such that $V=D(f)$ for some $f\in A_U$, with restriction $\varphi:A_U\to A_V$, there exist a $\varphi$-semilinear map $b:NA_U\to NA_V$, a chain map $a:P_U\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P_V)$, and a chain map $k:P_U\otimes_{A_U}NA_U\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P_V\otimes_{A_V}NA_V)$ satisfying $sM_V(\pi_Va_0x)=\operatorname{res}_M(sM_U(\pi_Ux))$, $sN_V(by)=\operatorname{res}_N(sN_Uy)$, $k_j(x\otimes y)=a_j(x)\otimes b(y)$, and $\operatorname{res}_Q(c_Uz)=c_V(e(H_n(k)(z)))$ for every $z$. Here $\pi_U$ and $\pi_V$ are the augmentations, and $e:H_n(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P_V\otimes_{A_V}NA_V))\simeq\operatorname{Res}_\varphi H_n(P_V\otimes_{A_V}NA_V)$ is the exact restriction-of-scalars homology comparison. Then this last restriction equation holds for every supplied $b,a,k$ satisfying those same augmentation, coefficient and pure-tensor equations, for every such inclusion and every $z$.

source.place: Tag 00LS(2), algebra.tex, lemma-compare-resolutions: inductive comparison homotopy; projective version proved with the same lifting property, then tensoring its components. Mathlib Homotopy.homologyMap_eq supplies homology invariance.

proof.text: Choose the witnessed b0,a0,k0 for the fixed basic inclusion. The two coefficient equations have the same right-hand side. Injectivity of sN_V therefore gives b0=b. Likewise injectivity of sM_V makes pi_V a0_0 = pi_V a_0. These cancellations are written directly in the public theorem.

Restrict the augmented P_V complex along phi. Exactness of restriction of scalars preserves its exact short complexes at degree zero and every positive degree. Subtract the two maps a0 and a. Their degree-zero difference vanishes under the augmentation. Lift it through d_1 by projectivity of (P_U)_0. At step j subtract the previously constructed homotopy component composed with d_j; the chain-map and preceding homotopy equations imply that the remainder lands in ker(d_j). Exactness and projectivity of (P_U)_j lift it through d_(j+1). The local augmented_lift_homotopy helper implements this induction using ShortComplex.Exact.liftFromProjective and Homotopy.mkInductive. The restricted target terms need not be projective. This is the argument of Tag 00LS(2) with projectivity in place of freeness.

For each homotopy component H_jl use TensorProduct.map to define x tensor y -> H_jl(x) tensor b(y), viewed as an A_U-linear map into restriction of scalars. Both factors are phi-semilinear, so the map is balanced. Its vanishing outside the homotopy degree follows from H.zero and zero tensor y=0. On pure tensors, the differential identity reduces to H.comm followed by (x+xprime) tensor y=x tensor y+xprime tensor y. TensorProduct.ext extends the equality to all elements. Thus the local tensor_resolution_lift_homotopy helper gives a homotopy k0~k, completely proved from Mathlib. The differential calculation uses Mathlib Homotopy.prevD_chainComplex directly; the duplicate local prevD_chain helper was removed in the repair.

Homotopy.homologyMap_eq gives H_n(k0)=H_n(k). Substitute this equality in the witnessed naturality equation. The same restriction-of-scalars homology comparison e and the same coordinate c_V occur on both sides, so the required equation follows immediately.

lean.statement:
theorem qcoh_ordinary_tensor_resolution_comparison_independence
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (M N : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
    [M.IsQuasicoherent] [N.IsQuasicoherent]
    (MA NA : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens, ModuleCat.{u} (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u))
    (sM : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens, MA U ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, U.1)] M.val.obj (op U.1))
    (sN : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens, NA U ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, U.1)] N.val.obj (op U.1))
    (P : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens, ProjectiveResolution (MA U))
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (q : K ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj M)
    (hK : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := Y.sheaf) K) (hq : QuasiIso q) (n : ℕ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory Y.sheaf
    let S := CochainComplex.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let Q := (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K (S.obj N)
      (curriedTensor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)))).homology
        (-(n : ℤ))
    ∀ c : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens,
        ((((tensorRight (NA U)).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)).obj
          (P U).complex).homology n) ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, U.1)] Q.val.obj (op U.1),
      (∀ (V U : Y.affineOpens) (h : V.1 ≤ U.1)
        (_hbasic : ∃ f : Γ(Y, U.1), Y.basicOpen f = V.1),
        let φ := (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
        let TA := (tensorRight (NA U)).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
        let TC := (tensorRight (NA V)).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
        ∃ (b : NA U →ₛₗ[φ] NA V)
          (a : (P U).complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.down ℕ)).obj (P V).complex)
          (k : TA.obj (P U).complex ⟶
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)).obj
              (TC.obj (P V).complex)),
          (∀ x : (P U).complex.X 0,
            sM V ((P V).π.f 0 (a.f 0 x)) =
              M.val.map (homOfLE h).op (sM U ((P U).π.f 0 x))) ∧
          (∀ y : NA U, sN V (b y) = N.val.map (homOfLE h).op (sN U y)) ∧
          (∀ (j : ℕ) (x : (P U).complex.X j) (y : NA U),
            k.f j (x ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, U.1)] y) =
              (show (P V).complex.X j from a.f j x) ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, V.1)] (b y)) ∧
          let e := ((TC.obj (P V).complex).sc n).mapHomologyIso
            (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ)
          ∀ x, Q.val.map (homOfLE h).op (c U x) =
            c V (e.hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap k n x))) →
      ∀ (V U : Y.affineOpens) (h : V.1 ≤ U.1)
        (_hbasic : ∃ f : Γ(Y, U.1), Y.basicOpen f = V.1),
        let φ := (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
        let TA := (tensorRight (NA U)).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
        let TC := (tensorRight (NA V)).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)
        ∀ (b : NA U →ₛₗ[φ] NA V)
          (a : (P U).complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.down ℕ)).obj (P V).complex)
          (k : TA.obj (P U).complex ⟶
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)).obj
              (TC.obj (P V).complex)),
          (∀ x : (P U).complex.X 0,
            sM V ((P V).π.f 0 (a.f 0 x)) =
              M.val.map (homOfLE h).op (sM U ((P U).π.f 0 x))) →
          (∀ y : NA U, sN V (b y) = N.val.map (homOfLE h).op (sN U y)) →
          (∀ (j : ℕ) (x : (P U).complex.X j) (y : NA U),
            k.f j (x ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, U.1)] y) =
              (show (P V).complex.X j from a.f j x) ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, V.1)] (b y)) →
          let e := ((TC.obj (P V).complex).sc n).mapHomologyIso
            (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ)
          ∀ x, Q.val.map (homOfLE h).op (c U x) =
            c V (e.hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap k n x))
